title: Australian national and NSW emergency resources — verified primary-source shortlist
research_note: Directory-ready facts. Hours are included only where stated on the cited source. Re-check dynamic warning, evacuation-centre and disaster-assistance pages at point of publication/use.
global_safety_caveat: For an immediate or life-threatening emergency, call Triple Zero (000). Do not use non-emergency, advice, recovery or web resources as a substitute for emergency response. Give the call-taker your exact location and follow emergency-service directions.

resources.name: Triple Zero (000)
resources.scope: Primary emergency number for Police, Fire or Ambulance; calls are free.
resources.safety_caveat: Use for emergencies only. A mobile cannot reach the Emergency Call Service where there is no coverage from any mobile network.

resources.name: Emergency Relay Service / National Relay Service (NRS)
resources.scope: For people who are d/Deaf or have hearing/speech difficulty to contact Police, Fire or Ambulance through the NRS. NRS Chat, SMS Relay, NRS Captions, Voice Relay and TTY emergency calls receive queue priority.
resources.hours: NRS is available 24/7 except Video Relay; Video Relay hours are limited.
resources.safety_caveat: Video Relay is not recommended for emergency calls: it cannot be identified/prioritised as emergency and operates only limited hours. Internet/mobile-based relay may be less reliable than 106 and may not identify caller/location. For a TTY, dial 106 first.

resources.name: NSW State Emergency Service (NSW SES)
resources.scope: Emergency assistance for flood, storm or tsunami, including storm/wind/fallen-tree damage. Requests are prioritised.
resources.safety_caveat: If anyone is trapped or injured, call 000. The online contact form is not monitored for storm/flood emergencies; call 132 500.

resources.name: Police Assistance Line
resources.scope: Non-urgent police assistance, minor-crime reporting and general enquiries.
resources.safety_caveat: For emergencies or a crime in progress, call 000 instead.

resources.name: Poisons Information Centre
resources.scope: Expert phone advice for suspected exposure to poisons, including medicines, chemicals, cleaning products, bites and stings.
resources.safety_caveat: Call promptly; do not wait for symptoms. If someone has stopped breathing or collapsed, call 000 for an ambulance.

resources.name: healthdirect helpline
resources.scope: Health advice from a registered nurse for any health concern.
resources.safety_caveat: For urgent medical help, call 000.

resources.name: Lifeline crisis support
resources.scope: Confidential crisis support with a trained crisis supporter; text is also available at 0477 13 11 14.
resources.safety_caveat: If life is in danger, call 000.

resources.name: 1800RESPECT
resources.scope: National counselling, information and support for people impacted by domestic, family or sexual violence. Text: 0458 737 732; online chat and video call are also offered.
resources.safety_caveat: If in immediate danger, call 000. Calls/texts may appear on a phone bill; consider safety when contacting the service.

resources.name: Kids Helpline
resources.scope: Free, confidential phone and online-chat counselling for children and young people aged 5–25.

resources.name: NSW Mental Health Line
resources.scope: Free statewide advice, triage and connection to NSW Health mental health services; a trained professional completes a brief assessment and recommends appropriate care.
resources.language_access: For another language, call TIS National 131 450 and ask to be connected. Relay options are listed on the source page.
resources.safety_caveat: Not a one-off counselling service. If someone is in immediate danger, call 000 or attend an emergency department.

resources.name: Service NSW — emergencies and natural disasters
resources.scope: Disaster preparation/recovery information, personalised support pathways, relief/grants information and replacement-document help; includes support-hub information.
resources.safety_caveat: In an emergency, call 000; for flood/storm/tsunami assistance, call NSW SES 132 500.

resources.name: Temporary and emergency housing / Link2Home
resources.scope: Link2Home helps people who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Service NSW/recovery centres can help disaster-affected residents access accommodation support.

resources.name: Legal Aid NSW — Disaster Response Legal Service
resources.scope: Free legal help after bushfire, storm or flood: insurance claims/disputes, tenancy/housing, disaster grants, financial hardship, Centrelink, work rights and documents.

resources.name: Bureau of Meteorology — NSW warnings summary
resources.scope: Official current NSW weather-warning summary; automatically refreshes when warnings are issued.
resources.safety_caveat: Read the linked warning in full and follow local emergency-service directions.

resources.name: Bureau of Meteorology — national warning phone service
resources.scope: Latest weather warnings by phone.

resources.name: Live Traffic NSW
resources.scope: Transport for NSW official real-time road incidents, closures and changed conditions; a text-to-speech Traffic Info Line and operator assistance are available.
resources.safety_caveat: Always read individual incident advice/restrictions and do not drive into floodwater or a closed road.

resources.name: NSW SES evacuation centres
resources.scope: Current evacuation-centre locations and opening hours; the page also gives evacuation guidance.
resources.safety_caveat: Centres open only during emergencies and status changes. Follow evacuation instructions immediately; check routes via Live Traffic. For fires, consult NSW RFS as directed by the page.

resources.name: NSW SES accessibility resources
resources.scope: Flood/storm/tsunami planning resources for low/no hearing or vision, disability/mobility, intellectual disability, mental health conditions, carers and Easy Read; includes Auslan and NRS information.
resources.safety_caveat: Create a tailored plan and support network before an emergency; plan backup power/transport for life-sustaining and mobility equipment.

resources.name: NSW SES — household pets emergency planning
resources.scope: Pet evacuation planning and a 3–7-day animal emergency-kit checklist.
resources.safety_caveat: Plan to take pets, but evacuation centres may not always be available or suitable for animals; arrange alternative safe options. Assistance animals have separate access guidance.

resources.name: NSW SES — assistance animals emergency planning
resources.scope: Planning guidance and kit checklist for assistance animals during evacuation.
resources.safety_caveat: The NSW SES page says people should not be denied transport or evacuation-centre access because of an assistance animal; plan travel and specific animal needs in advance.

resources.name: NSW Government — Get Ready Animals
resources.scope: Emergency planning for companion animals, larger pets, horses and livestock, including a Pet Ready Plan.
resources.safety_caveat: Never leave a pet behind; secure/transport it early. Not all evacuation centres allow pets, so plan alternatives.

resources.name: Translating and Interpreting Service (TIS National)
resources.scope: Immediate phone interpreting for people with limited or no English; the operator connects the caller and an interpreter to the organisation requested. Most interpreting services are free to non-English speakers.
resources.hours: Immediate phone interpreting: 24 hours a day, every day of the year
resources.safety_caveat: For immediate danger, call 000 rather than waiting for an interpreter connection. Mobile calls may cost more.
resources.verification: Page fetched 2026-10-18 with WebFetch; the 131 450 number, 24-hour availability, steps and cost statement were read on the page.

resources.name: Translating and Interpreting Service (TIS National) pathway for NSW mental-health support
resources.scope: Interpreter connection pathway: ask TIS to ring NSW Mental Health Line 1800 011 511.
resources.safety_caveat: For immediate danger, call 000 rather than waiting for a support connection.

resources.name: NSW Health — respiratory illness (flu, COVID-19 and RSV)
resources.scope: Vaccination, stay-home, mask and testing advice; links to weekly respiratory surveillance reports. No symptom triage or phone numbers on the page.
resources.safety_caveat: For urgent medical help, call 000.

resources.scope: COVID-19 vaccination, testing and symptoms guide.
